```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a sourced zero-cash acquisition path that fits the 90-day goal. Instatus's Product Hunt launch (559 upvotes, Product of the Day) drove its first customer wave. Idea B's channels are generic and expensive: a $237 blended B2B SaaS cost-per-lead benchmark that is not specific to contractors, and a $0.01 to $10+ CPC range too wide to plan against. A bootstrapped solo operator cannot easily absorb that spend.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence is broader and fully sourced: four quotes with URLs, each naming specific price pain ($8 to $34 hike, $79 invoice, $20/mo for a hobby project). Idea B has only one sourced demand quote. Its second quote has no retrieved URL and counts as missing.",
    "Idea A's buyers are developers and small SaaS teams who self-serve on low-friction, low-price plans ($9 to $15/mo). That makes a first paying customer within 90 days more plausible. Idea B's buyers are described in its own brief as time-poor and skeptical of software. B also carries accuracy and trust risk, because an underbid AI estimate costs the contractor real money, and that raises the bar for a fast MVP to earn payment.",
    "Idea A's technical surface is shown to be buildable by one person, with sourced examples of solo builders shipping working clones on simple stacks. Idea B's claim that competitors like EstimationPro are run by single contractor-founders carries no source. B also admits that the crew-scheduling scope is unlikely to work within six weeks.",
    "Both ideas are crowded. Idea A is more saturated, with 10+ near-identical entrants and price compression toward $9/mo. But Idea B also faces at least seven direct competitors, and several of B's competitor prices are unpublished. Saturation therefore does not clearly favor B."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence effectively rests on a single Reddit quote ('1-2 hours per night writing quotes'). The second quote ('half your week driving around...') has no retrieved URL and is listed as unsourced. Willingness to pay is inferred only from competitor existence, and many of those competitors' prices are unpublished.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Idea A's demand quotes come largely from people who chose to build their own monitor rather than pay, which weakens them as willingness-to-pay evidence. Idea A's saturation and reliability burden are serious. Idea B offers higher per-customer revenue ($50 to $125/mo) that could offset its thin evidence if a narrow trade wedge works. The pick rests mainly on Idea A's cheaper, sourced acquisition path and better-sourced demand signals, not on a clear win."
}
```
